THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
Since the above appeals are arising out of the same accident, both appeals are clubbed, heard together and are being disposed of by this judgment.
2. The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.2,90,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, is in appeal.
3. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.
The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered cut lacerated wound over chin and pain near left thigh.

5. The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation:
Sl. Amount  Particulars No. in (Rs.)
1. Pain and sufferings 30,000 2.

Medical expenses 2,09,742 Loss of income during the laid 3. 10,000 up period 4. Conveyance, food, nourishment, 15,000 attendant charges 5. Loss of amenities in life 25,000 Total 2,89,742 Rounded of 2,90,000 L Sowbhagya vs L Veerabhadraiah on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1484709/
3 6. The Tribunal has noted that the claimant was working as a teacher and therefore, there was no loss of future income.

The Tribunal also noticed that the medical evidence indicated that she had suffered permanent C/W MFA 4146 of 2017 physical disability at 7% to the whole body and she had lost ten teeth which resulted in difficulty in chewing hard food and also difficulty in speaking.

In my view, having regard to the fact that the claimant was 47 years of teacher, who had suffered loss of ten teeth, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.30,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

7. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,25,000/- towards loss of amenities, as against the sum of Rs.25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

8. The sums awarded as 'medical expenses' by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence,
does not call for modification and hence confirmed.

9. The sums awarded under the heads of 'loss of income during laid up period' and 'conveyance,
nourishing C/W MFA 4146 of 2017 food and attendant charges' are also just and proper and do not call modification and hence confirmed.

10. Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
 As As  awarded awarded  Sl. Compensation under  by the by this  No. different Heads  Tribunal Court  (Rs.) (Rs.)
1 . Pain and sufferings 30,000 1,00,000

2. Medical expenses 2,09,742 2,09,742  Loss of income during  3. 10,000 10,000  the laid up period  Conveyance, food,
 4. nourishment, attendant 15,000 15,000  charges  5. Loss of amenities in life 25,000 1,25,000  Total 2,89,742 4,59,742  Rounded of 2,90,000 4,60,000 L Sowbhagya vs L Veerabhadraiah on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1484709/
4  C/W  MFA 4146 of 2017 11.
Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.4,60,000/- as against Rs.2,90,000/-, along with interest from the date of petition till its realization.
12. This claim is by the daughter of the claimant in MFA No.4145/2017, who was aged 18 years old.
13. The Tribunal taking note of the fact that the claimant did not suffer any permanent disability, as thought it fit to award a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- as global compensation.
14. In my view, it would be appropriate to enhance the global compensation Rs.1,25,000/- in addition to medical expenses of Rs.33,398/- incurred by the claimant.
15. Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.1,58,398/- as against Rs.1,00,000/-, along with interest from the date of petition till its realization.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
17. The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.
18. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
19. The appeals are accordingly allowed in part.
